Read the worked example before attempting the exercises. A quadratic equation is any equation that can be rearranged into the standard form ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero with a not equal to zero, and while some quadratics factor neatly over the integers, most do not, so you will need the quadratic formula or the method of completing the square, both of which are derived from the same underlying identity and both of which will give the same two roots whenever the discriminant is positive.
